A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IFMET study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-J mechanistic investigations, causal interventions, and IFMET knowledge-editing experiments on MQuAKE, including additional appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds component ablations, LLaMA-2 evaluations, model-generated editing prompts, and editing-time measurements.

M1.justification: The two-stage editor, PMET-based Search/Calculate procedures, losses, and weight updates remain unchanged. v3 adds an alternative procedure that obtains supporting knowledge from the model itself to construct multi-hop editing prompts, alongside the existing WikiData procedure (Appendix D.1 and Table 13).

E1.justification: MQuAKE remains the benchmark family. v3 constructs paraphrase and neighborhood sets from a MQuAKE-3K subset, extending evaluation to reworded queries and preservation of neighboring facts (Appendix F). COUNTERFACT supplies the construction approach, rather than becoming an additional evaluated benchmark.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain their baseline methods. FT already appears in v1's appendix CoT tables, which become v3 Table 3; MeLLo remains in the batch comparison in v3 Figure 7. The new analyses reuse existing comparison methods, chiefly PMET.

E3.justification: v3 introduces LLaMA-2-7B experiments and component-ablation protocols using edit batches of 1 and 100, with efficacy, paraphrase, specificity, and editing-time measurements. Existing GPT-J few-shot and CoT evaluations remain; moving the CoT results into the main text does not establish a changed protocol.

E4.justification: v3 adds ablations of the first editing stage, multi-hop prompts, token position, and layer depth, plus LLaMA-2 causal interventions, prompt-source comparisons, and timing analyses (Tables 5 and 7-9; Figure 6). The earlier Pre/Post analysis remains, but its batch-100 row is omitted from v3 Table 2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The added relative percentage changes and average editing times do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial ablation, LLaMA-2, prompt-source, and timing results. The main CoT scores are retained from v1's appendix. In matched Table 4, IFMET+CoT's unedited-answer average changes from 21.62 to 21.32 and its Mid score from 30.51 to 28.20. Figure 7 also changes some batch results and plots zeros for batched ROME entries that v1 marked unavailable.

T1.justification: The LogitLens information definition, causal-intervention equations and approximation, key-value assumptions, and IFMET optimization/update formulas are retained. The added evaluation metrics do not introduce new theoretical results or substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstracts, contribution lists, and conclusions retain the same central claims: implicit multi-hop retrieval uses deeper MLPs, shallow editing leaves relevant knowledge unchanged, and IFMET improves multi-hop recall through shallow and deep editing. The revised introduction makes the existing hypotheses more explicit.

C2.justification: Appendices F-G add substantive interpretations of component necessity, transfer to LLaMA-2, and model-generated prompts. They also acknowledge specificity loss and editing-time overhead, qualifying v1's largely benefit-focused discussion. For example, Table 7 reports specificity of 69.87 for IFMET versus 78.60 for PMET and discusses the resulting tradeoff.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the model-generated prompt template, a limit of one to five prompts per case, and the absence of additional filtering for that variant. It also reports per-edit times. Existing WikiData queries, GPT-J layer ranges, optimization settings, and editing equations are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A is largely unchanged. New Appendix G.1 positions locate-then-edit against weight-preserving/RAG approaches through internal-knowledge, retrieval-cost, and security arguments, adding Jin et al. (2024) and Upadhayay et al. (2024). The Levy et al. (2017) citation is removed.

P1.justification: The introduction is reorganized around explicit hypotheses, Section 3 becomes a sequence of three research questions, and the method and experimental narratives are substantially rewritten. Existing appendix material is reorganized into separate dataset, intervention, method, settings, results, and prompt sections, alongside the new analyses.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main text, merges v1 Tables 5-6 into Table 3, splits Table 4 into two panels, and redraws the batch comparison as Figure 7. It adds ablation, timing, and prompt tables and a LLaMA-2 heatmap, while enlarging or redisplaying several retained figures.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's lack of component ablations, validation beyond GPT-J, and assessment of editing side effects. The new experiments strengthen attribution of the gains and expose specificity and runtime costs. These benefits outweigh limited reporting defects, including Table 8's incorrect percentage-baseline caption and runtime ratios in Appendix G that disagree with Table 9.
